answers.answer: Roll one die simultaneously per held office card, adding one per fatigue and one extra for Chairman. Modified 1–2 does nothing; 3–4 adds fatigue; 5+ retires the officeholder. Move the member to Pensioners, flip the card to Vacant Offices, and return its fatigue to supply.
answers.evidence: London Season—Attrition: ‘Modified 1–2: nothing; 3–4: add fatigue; 5+: retire. Move retiree to Pensioners, flip card into Vacant Offices, return its fatigue to supply.’

answers.answer: Only players who retired at least one pensioner select or discard one displayed card, ordered by descending actual retirement spending; ties go to most total windows including new prizes, then clockwise from PM. Do not replace cards during selection; if the display empties, skip remaining eligible players. Then discard all remaining cards, refill exactly three (prestige faceup, blackmail facedown), and return unused Pensioners to supplies.
answers.evidence: London Season—Prestige: ‘Players who retired at least one pensioner’; descending spending and stated tiebreakers; ‘If the display becomes empty, immediately skip’; refill exactly three; unused Pensioners return to supplies.

answers.answer: At phase start, check whether the opportunity marker matched the chosen main action: if so, that action may be taken twice. Then move the marker onto the chosen main action. Only the latest passed extra-action law may grant a later extra action; it is never doubled and does not move the marker. With four vacant offices and a doubled Enlist Writer, place three writers total (the vacancy bonus adds one writer once that turn).
answers.evidence: Family: steps 1–4; Enlist Writer: ‘With at least four vacant offices, place one additional writer once this turn, so a doubled Writer action can place three total.’

answers.answer: After all family actions, while both Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and reduce Debt by one, repeating as able. With no Debt, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible while preserving order. Seeking a share pays the applicant-space price to the bank; it does not put family cash into Company treasuries.
answers.evidence: Family—New Company shares: rightmost applicant moves to Court as Debt is lowered; no Debt means slide applicants right preserving order. Seek Share: pay bank; ‘never pays family cash into Company treasuries.’

answers.answer: Fill vacancies in ascending number on card backs. Own-family hiring requires verbal consent from every other player represented in that office’s candidate pool; Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt. On promotion, transfer fatigue to the new card and put the old card, vacant, into ascending hiring order. If there is no candidate or the hirer is vacant, skip it; it remains vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.
answers.evidence: Hiring: ‘Fill vacant offices in ascending number’; own-family consent and exceptions; promotion fatigue transfer; no candidate/hirer means skip and office stays vacant.

answers.answer: The former Chairman announces the number of shares needed for a pure majority (more than half current shares). Shareholders may campaign; the first candidate backed by players controlling that many shares wins. If no candidate gets support, former Chairman selects any shareholder, including self. The winner’s Company share moves into the Chairman slot and still counts for dividends, majority, and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in a firm.
answers.evidence: Hiring—Chairman election: pure majority and campaign procedure; fallback selection; elected share ‘still counts as a share’ but cannot be traded or invested.

answers.answer: For an ordinary Company-office check, commit resources and any cash from that office’s treasury (cash goes to bank), gather dice, subtract penalties, and roll; use the lowest die. 1–2 succeeds, 3–4 fails and may be retried if resources and office limits permit, 5–6 catastrophically fails: no further office actions, return holder to supply, discard fatigue, and flip card to Vacant Offices. Do not take a dead action with no effect or chance of success, such as trading with no ship or deploying without dice merely to risk officer losses. Commander/firm procedures can modify checks.
answers.evidence: Company Operation—Success checks: treasury payment, lowest die outcomes, retry and catastrophe effects, and dead-action examples.

answers.answer: Chairman may add up to three Debt freely, receiving £5 Balance per advance. Each further advance needs consent of players controlling a majority of Company shares (Chairman counts); never advance past the Debt track end. Chairman must then allocate all Balance to other offices’ treasuries, reducing Balance by the transfers; borrowing and allocation may be interleaved while respecting the borrowing limit. Existing office cash stays there.
answers.evidence: Actions—Chairman: ‘May add up to three Debt freely’; additional advances need majority-share consent; never pass track end; ‘allocate all Balance’ to other treasuries.

answers.answer: Manager of Shipping must spend treasury until £2 or less remains. Lease an extra ship for £2; fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without its owner’s consent; buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Put each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China if it exists. Extra ships return to supply at Refresh.
answers.evidence: Actions—Manager of Shipping: treasury stopping point, costs, fitting consent, Company-ship prerequisite and destination; Refresh table returns extra ships.

answers.answer: Declare home region plus only regions reachable through open orders and available ship capacity; subtract one die per declared nonhome region. Each £1 from the President’s treasury buys a die; failures may be retried if affordable, catastrophe removes President. Successful Trade fills at most one order per ship in that Presidency’s sea zone, without exhausting ships. First writer goes to home port; each later order extends this Trade’s own connected route. Writers from other Presidencies cannot extend it, and writers do not limit capacity: after using writers, fill remaining capacity with filled-order tokens. Cannot fill another President’s home region. Company Balance gets each order’s printed value, or half rounded down if a firm filled it this turn; President earns £1/order and writer owners £1 per writer. At most one successful Trade per President per turn.
answers.evidence: Actions—Presidency operations and Trade: declaration, dice penalty, retry/catastrophe, one-success limit, capacity, route, writers/tokens, protected homes and payouts.

answers.answer: Deploy may target the Commander’s home region, any associated region, or a region bordering an associated region, but not another home region or another Presidency’s Company-controlled region. A Company target must have unrest or a closed order. Exhaust officers/regiments for one die each and alliances for their printed dice; subtract target strength plus all other regions in its empire (target only once), while Company-controlled defense strength is zero. After each attempt, owners roll one die per officer exhausted in that attempt; each 6 removes that officer. Regiments do not roll losses. Noncatastrophic failures can retry with remaining resources.
answers.evidence: Actions—Commanders and Deploy, steps 1–3: eligible targets, die sources and penalties, retry, and officer loss rolls.

answers.answer: On success, loot is £4 per target tower plus faceup loot modifier, with minimum equal to surviving officers used in this attempt plus one. Distribute repeated £1 cycles: Commander gets £1 for self plus each used surviving officer; other families clockwise get £1 per used surviving officer; bank last gets £1 per used regiment and alliance piece. Commander gets one trophy per target tower. Then remove target tower/dome, open all orders, clear unrest; for a newly controlled region place its control token and Governor overlay on map and send only the office card to Vacant Offices (no Governorship if Governor General is in play). Move Elephant fully inside if it faced outward. Catastrophe returns half Commander-family trophies rounded up and Commander to supply; exhausted officers still check losses.
answers.evidence: Actions—Commanders and Deploy: successful loot/trophy and control procedure; catastrophe rule.

answers.answer: Each attempt rolls the current printed dice pool without penalty, then reduces that pool by one regardless of result. Success pays £1, or £2 if the immediately previous roll was unsuccessful, and requires exactly one benefit: build a ship, commission a regiment, or tax. Building takes two successful stages: first place partial ship in Governor’s region; another success completes it into the President’s sea zone. Regiment goes in associated Army. Tax adds unsplit £2 to Company Balance or that President’s treasury; each Tax after the first this turn adds unrest. Every unsuccessful roll adds one unrest; catastrophe also removes holder normally. Continue with shrinking pool until stop, no dice, or catastrophe.
answers.evidence: Actions—Governors: Administer: shrinking pool, preceding-failure bonus, options and destinations, unrest and stopping.

answers.answer: Company first pays £1 per existing Debt, Army officer/regiment, and sea-zone ship (including China); Commanders are excluded. If Balance is insufficient, take £5 emergency loans, advancing Debt one each until track end; loans continue even at max Debt. Newly added Debt has no current-turn expense. Set Balance to zero after loans. One or two loans lower Standing one; three or more lower it two. Then compare remaining Balance with expectations for current Standing and lower Standing one if short. Chairman may then pay affordable dividends, one cash per share, giving each share owner £1 including Chairman; if total paid is strictly greater than expectations, raise Standing one.
answers.evidence: Revenue: Expenses, Expectations, Dividends; emergency loan, Standing, expense and payout rules.

answers.answer: A normal Crisis attacking a Company region resolves primary target first, then secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest, in Bombay→Madras→Bengal Army order; each Commander chooses order among their associated regions. Primary Invasion/Rebellion strength is normal attack strength plus unrest in its target. Each secondary attack strength is only that region’s unrest. Associated Commander exhausts active Army pieces totaling strength, or as much as possible; the printed defense rule says defense succeeds only if newly exhausted pieces equal strength. Successful defense clears all target unrest and gives Commander a trophy; if it stopped a normal primary Invasion, also remove one attacker tower if possible. Vacant Commander is replaced for this defense by Military Affairs, or Chairman if Military Affairs vacant; the acting player gets/loses no trophies. Excess indivisible alliance defense remains unresolved in the summary.
answers.evidence: Events in India—Attacks on Company: attack order and strengths, matching defense and effects; FAQ: ‘excess alliance strength in defense’ explicitly unresolved.

answers.answer: Before voting, PM sets the proposed policy by moving dial clockwise or counterclockwise to the first matching policy space; it determines target and consequence. Starting support comes from law. Vote at −1 or less fails: discard law, resolve dilemma’s If Failed text, Opposition Leader returns token and takes PM dial, new PM shifts proposed policy one space either way and resolves that adjacent policy. At zero or more it passes: place law with passed laws, PM takes passed-law token, resolve chosen policy and then immediate law effects. Support-zero therefore passes. Restore voting cards after either result. A vote’s card-specific votes are only usable once across all rounds. The summary does not specify a separate policy movement on successful ordinary passage beyond the selected policy/effects.
answers.evidence: Parliament Meets—Resolution: threshold and failure/pass consequences and order; policy selection is stated before Voting.

answers.answer: In 1758 and Long 1710, at turn start before London Season, PM may call a special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. Use ordinary voting and support threshold, with exceptions: no policy accompanies it, PM may vote against, and failure neither removes PM nor discards the law. Passing lowers Debt one per two current Debt, sets Standing to S, gives PM a passed-law token, and activates firms. Failure increases Company-share scoring value by flipping/placing the Court VP token, up to ±3. 1813 starts deregulated; 1710 has no deregulation procedures.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: special votes at very start; Setup scenario scope; Deregulation: trigger spaces and pass/fail rules.

answers.answer: A player managing no firm may form one by contributing one eligible Company share (returned to supply) or flipping a workshop to invested side, flipping their board to firm charter, and placing a family member as first firm share; firm starts at leftmost Value and receives £5 from bank into London. With manager’s consent, the same contributions invest in an existing firm and add £5 from bank to London. Ten firm shares maximum; contributions beyond cap still add £5 but no shares. Cannot contribute Chairman share; cannot use Company shares at all while Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space; shares created this turn cannot be reinvested even after being traded. Invested workshops stay invested and yield neither bonus nor Company-failure VP, including after firm failure.
answers.evidence: Deregulation—Firms phase: investments: formation, funding, eligibility, ten-share limit and invested workshop effects.

answers.answer: Each firm makes exactly one trade attempt per turn. Managers secretly choose trade zone/home port and a London-cash bid (home port may be closed), or Hobnob (no bid/trade/dividends). Reveal bids together; reveal strategy at its Presidency before actions, roll one die per £1 bid paid to bank; at least one 1/2 allows trade. Initiative is ships minus successful dice. Successful President Trade has initiative computed similarly; then lowest initiative fills first. President decides ties among traders; if President vacant or never trades, firms act after Commander/Governors, and Chairman breaks initiative ties. Firm fills up to ships+1 orders along own route from home port, each order once; can refill orders others filled this turn. Place filled tokens, revenue to India. Previously filled order pays half listed revenue rounded down. Raise Value one space per full £6 added to India this turn.
answers.evidence: Deregulation—Firm strategies and competing trade: attempt, bids/checks, initiative, order, capacity, repeat-fill revenue and value.

answers.answer: At start of Revenue, firms pay £1 per charter ship plus the higher of share count or firm Value, using either or both treasuries. If unable, dissolve unless rescued: shares go to Debtor’s Prison (−1 VP each), ships to shipyards, charter flips back; workshops remain invested. Rescue by emergency investments under normal contribution rules—even at ten shares, cash may still be contributed—pay expenses, lose remaining cash, and lower Value one per rescue investment; or emergency merger with only one other firm, with all involved shareholder consent and the other firm paying its own expenses first, then endangered firm’s unpaid costs. After expenses, manager may pay dividends only from India: £1 per share plus £1 manager for each dividend. Waiving requires shareholder choice and manager consent; record total actual payout on Company Balance track. Active non-Hobnob firm paying none records zero; Hobnob retains prior marker. Sweep remaining India cash to London.
answers.evidence: Deregulation—Firm expenses, rescue and dividends: expense formula, dissolution, rescue and payout rules.

answers.answer: Company Balance, VP and Vote tracks are unlimited. Other components are limited; when a supply runs out, complete as much as possible. Cash, trophy/passed-law tokens, dice and regiments may use proxies. All information, including discards and family cash, is public except facedown blackmail and firm strategies/bids while temporarily concealed during selection.
answers.evidence: Components—Limits: limited supply/proxies, unlimited tracks, public information and concealed exceptions.

answers.answer: Negotiations may trade enterprises, facedown blackmail, family cash, Company/firm shares and promise cards. Cannot trade officeholders, writers, officers, prizes, spouses, trophies, passed laws, played blackmail or PM dial; Chairman piece cannot transfer. When share changes family, replace its member with new owner’s family piece. Luxury VP adjusts with ownership. Blackmail may be shown privately but never traded faceup; once played it cannot be traded.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Negotiation: allowed/prohibited assets, share representation, luxury VP, blackmail restrictions; London Season says used blackmail cannot be traded.

answers.answer: Immediate transfers are binding; promises of future behavior are not, except printed promise cards can be called for their guaranteed effect if possible, subject to card timing/limits. If simultaneous calls cannot all be fulfilled, guarantor chooses which to fulfill. A promise card may be traded to a third party or back to guarantor. Transferred resources cannot activate twice (example: workshop bonus already paid this phase is not paid again after sale). The summary does not state a general numerical limit on calls beyond each card’s printed timing and limits.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Negotiation: binding status, promise calls, simultaneous impossible calls, card timing/limits and transferred resource activation.

answers.answer: Use the chosen scenario’s player setup cards and add three extra cards for five players or six for six players; shuffle and deal evenly. Take listed cash, enterprises and positions, and place holdings according to the setup placement table, including matching office cards for officeholders. Each starting luxury gives 2 VP. Shuffle prestige and blackmail together and deal three display cards, prestige faceup and blackmail facedown; shuffle remaining laws.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3–4 and listed setup holding placement table.

answers.answer: Game ends after scenario’s final turn or when Standing reaches failure. Failure is immediate normally; if during Events in India, finish that phase before Final Scoring; if legislation causes failure, finish the vote first. Once game over, stop negotiations, promise calls and blackmail unless a card explicitly permits final-scoring use; during Final Scoring no negotiations or promise calls are allowed.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: ending and phase-completion rules; negotiations and promise calls barred in Final Scoring.

answers.answer: Final Power totals enterprise/share power on current Power track (bottom two positions zero), plus one per passed-law token and trophy, two for PM, and printed card power including faceup/facedown blackmail and applicable spouse. Awards depend on final turn: turns 1–3: 3/1 VP, 4–6: 5/2, 7–8: 8/4 for first/second. Tied first players each get only lower award and no other award; tied second players get none. Highest final VP wins; ties break by most windows, then clockwise from PM.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions—Power award, tie rules and final victory tiebreaker.

answers.answer: At Final Scoring, first score firm shares and allow each shareholder one eligible special retirement regardless of Company outcome. If Company survives, add current Court VP per Company share; if it fails, subtract that value per share and add 1 VP per uninvested workshop. Then survival permits office attrition and pensioner retirement without prestige; failure instead draws and resolves one Company failure card. Invested workshops never get failure VP.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: Company survival/failure branches and special retirements; firm investment rule excludes invested workshops from failure VP.

answers.answer: Spouses usually add VP, impose permanent restrictions and cannot be transferred. Required enterprise/share trades happen immediately on taking a spouse. Retirement discounts can stack and are personal; each is usable once during London Season and once during Final Scoring. Discounts reduce actual retirement spending and thus prestige priority.
answers.evidence: London Season: spouses and retirement discounts; Special Retirement firm rule repeats spouse discount eligibility.

answers.answer: If shipyard returns through Violet Effingham or unpaid tax, its fitted ship stays in play. The shipyard cannot be bought while its matching ship remains in play; it becomes buyable after that ship returns.
answers.evidence: London Season: ‘Returned shipyard rule’ explicitly covers Violet Effingham and unpaid tax.

answers.answer: Enlist Writer and Enlist Officer have no stated cash cost: place a family member in any Presidency’s Writers box or Officers-in-Training, respectively. Purchase Luxury costs £4 to bank; gain luxury, 2 VP while owned, window icon, social enterprise. Purchase Shipyard costs £2 to bank; place matching ship unfitted on shipyard; shipping enterprise, one vote and £1 bonus while fitted. Purchase Workshop costs £5 to bank; manufacturing enterprise, two votes and £1 bonus; worth 1 VP on Company failure unless invested. Seek Share costs the selected empty queue-space price (£2, £3, £3, £4 or £5) to bank and creates an applicant, not immediately a share. No income is stated for Writers or Officers themselves.
answers.evidence: Family action table: each listed cost/effect and Company failure scoring.

answers.answer: If a family piece must be placed and none is in supply, take one from any of that player’s prizes and lose that prize’s printed VP; this also applies to firm-share creation. If no Family action is possible, take none and return opportunity marker to supply.
answers.evidence: Family phase: forced prize-piece reuse and no-action rule.

answers.answer: If Court is empty, former Chairman automatically returns as Chairman, placing a member from supply or, if necessary and possible, from a prize and losing that prize’s VP. If placement is impossible, there is no Chairman. The summary gives this as the empty-Court rule; it does not add another fallback.
answers.evidence: Hiring—Chairman election: ‘If Court is empty, former Chairman automatically returns’; supply/prize piece and impossible-placement result.

answers.answer: Shareholders elect Chairman. Chairman hires Director (choose current officeholder other than Chairman/Governor; if all offices vacant, any writer), Manager of Shipping (any writer), and Military Affairs (Presidential Commander, else any officer, else trainee). Director hires President from a writer or Governor associated with that Presidency. Associated President hires Governor from writer or officer in its region; Commander is ineligible. Chairman hires China Superintendent from any writer immediately upon creation. Governor General replaces Director and is hired the same way as Director. If no candidate or hirer exists, ordinary hiring skips the vacancy; Commander appointments use Army-piece eligibility and are exempt from Nepotism.
answers.evidence: Hiring office table and no-candidate/hirer rule; China and Governor General entries.

answers.answer: Director may make repeated Special Envoy checks, each costing £1 treasury per die and with no penalty. Success opens one closed order in a non-Company region, or opens China by placing its Superintendent overlay/card; Chairman then immediately hires any writer. After all Envoys, Director may make up to two transfers, each one writer or ship between any Presidencies/sea zones, including China once created. Transfers cannot happen until Envoys are finished. The summary does not specify an additional Special Envoy action beyond these effects.
answers.evidence: Actions—Director of Trade: Special Envoy check effects, China hiring, transfer limit and timing.

answers.answer: Military Affairs first may make up to two transfers of an officer or regiment between Armies, each remaining in the top half. Then assign every trainee to any Army’s top half. Finally appoint Commanders: if vacant or another family has more total pieces in the Army than incumbent’s family, choose among families with the most pieces; move chosen officer to Commander slot and previous Commander to top as officer. A tie with incumbent’s family does not replace them. Nepotism does not apply.
answers.evidence: Actions—Military Affairs: stated sequence, eligibility, replacement and Nepotism exemption.

answers.answer: Each President chooses order of its Commander, Governors and Trade, giving each position an opportunity; Commander/Governors may decline. A position completes all actions before next, and Trade cannot interrupt another position. If President is vacant, Chairman sets order only and cannot Trade or approve local alliance purchases. The summary does not say the Chairman can take over a vacant President’s other actions.
answers.evidence: Actions—Presidency operations and Trade: order, declines, interruption, vacant-President limits.

answers.answer: Trade ships do not become exhausted. At nonfinal Refresh, writers return to their associated Presidency’s Writers box, using dividers to preserve affiliation; filled tokens and dividers return to supply. Fitted player ships keep fatigue. On final turn, Refresh is skipped.
answers.evidence: Presidency Trade: Trade does not exhaust ships; Upkeep and Refresh table and final-turn rule.

answers.answer: Commander first requests President’s treasury funds for printed-price local alliances, and President must approve purchase; put them in active/top Army half. Using an alliance for Deploy or defense exhausts the whole piece to bottom; its printed strength cannot be split and is usable once that turn. Unused active alliances also exhaust at Refresh and do not reactivate. Summary says alliances may defend, but expressly leaves unresolved whether excess indivisible strength (e.g. strength 2 against attack 1) counts as successful defense or how excess is treated.
answers.evidence: Actions—Commanders and Deploy: purchase, use and exhaustion; FAQ: excess alliance strength defense ruling is unresolved.

answers.answer: Deploying in an already Company-controlled target has Company defense penalty zero; if it has no tower and no faceup loot modifier, trophies are zero and loot uses the minimum of surviving participating officers plus one for the Commander. It still must be a legal target with unrest or a closed order and have dice/resources to make the check; the summary gives no alternative special penalty.
answers.evidence: Actions—Commanders and Deploy: Company region target rule and ‘Deploying in an already Company-controlled region’ special rule.

answers.answer: Two successful Build stages are needed: the first successful Administer option places a partial ship in the Governor’s region; a later successful Build completes it into the sea zone associated with Governor’s President. Governor-commissioned regiments go into that President’s associated Army, have officer-like strength, pay loot to bank and do not make officer-loss rolls.
answers.evidence: Actions—Governors: Administer: Build Company ship stages and Commission regiment destination/treatment.

answers.answer: China is created by successful Special Envoy or Envoy to China law; in either case Chairman immediately hires any writer. Its treasury holds ships, not cash. Shipping and Director may send ships there; they count Eastern for expenses, events, storms and laws. China acts after Bengal.
answers.evidence: Actions—China: creation, hiring, treasury, Eastern classification and turn order.

answers.answer: China may attempt Trade only once after Bengal. It rolls one die per ship and can act only if Company regions have at least one export icon. The summary does not give a repeat after failed check, so no repeat is supported. On success, count icons across Company-controlled regions only: Company Balance receives £4 per icon and Superintendent’s family receives £1 per icon from bank. Non-Company export icons earn nothing. No separate China Trade bonus is stated.
answers.evidence: Actions—Superintendent of Trade in China: once, dice/prerequisite, export count, amounts and recipients; no repeat or extra bonus specified.

answers.answer: When Governor General law creates the office, make Governors pensioners, remove overlays and partial ships, and return Governor/Director cards to box; replace Director with Governor General preserving holder and fatigue and place ribbon overlay. No new Governors/overlays are created on later conquest; printed Company symbols show controlled regions. On region loss, skip Governor Elimination. The summary does not state another special subsequent-conquest procedure beyond this.
answers.evidence: Actions—Governor General: law effects and subsequent conquest/region-loss differences.

answers.answer: Before Govern checks, add £3 Balance per Company region. May attempt Govern repeatedly, paying £1 treasury per die without penalty; every rolled 6 adds one unrest to each Company region even on success, and a failure adds another unrest to every Company region. Each success adds £1 per Company region and requires one benefit per region: complete Company ship into any sea zone including China, regiment into any Army, or £2 to Balance/any other office treasury (not own), adding unrest to a Company region. Tax unrest for multiple choices in the turn must be placed in different regions. At most one successful Govern per turn.
answers.evidence: Actions—Governor General: guaranteed revenue, dice/checks, unrest, success options and success limit.

answers.answer: For each player-owned ship in rolled storm zones, roll once: 1–2 nothing; 3–4 fatigue if unfatigued, sink if already fatigued; 5–6 sink. Company and extra ships are exempt. Sunk ship returns to shipyard unfatigued. China ships count Eastern. Firm ships face storms in their strategy zone; Hobnob ships are exempt.
answers.evidence: Events in India—Storms and Firm expenses/strategies: ship categories and effects.

answers.answer: When an order newly closes, return any writer there to its owner’s supply and flip a filled token to closed. If closure is instructed in a fully closed region, Cascade by closing all open orders directly connected to its orders; if a connected order is already closed, close that region’s northernmost open order instead. If there are no open orders, it also Cascades. A region can initiate only one Cascade per event tile, but can receive multiple Cascades’ effects.
answers.evidence: Events in India—Closing orders and Cascades: token/writer effect and full cascade conditions.

answers.answer: Turmoil closes the northernmost open order in the region shown by the top-stack tile; if all are closed, Cascade. Windfall pays owners £1 per writer on orders in that region and every bordering region. Shuffle causes Elephant’s March, then shuffles that tile with remaining draw stack and separately shuffles discards onto the top; if draw stack is empty, March last instead.
answers.evidence: Events in India event table: Turmoil, Windfall and Shuffle.

answers.answer: Leader uses the top-stack region. A sovereign region gains one tower. A dominated region instead rebels with the printed explosion modifier. Elephant moves only if it had been fully inside a Company region that successfully rebelled.
answers.evidence: Events in India—Leader entry.

answers.answer: If Elephant is on a border, Peace opens orders connected across its border and adds one tower to each touched non-Company region. If Elephant is fully within a region, instead open all that region’s orders and remove its unrest. Then March in either case.
answers.evidence: Events in India—Peace entry.

answers.answer: For non-Company Invasion, compare attacking sovereign’s whole empire strength plus event modifier against defender’s whole empire strength; attacker must be strictly greater, so equality fails. On success replace defender flag with attacker’s dominated flag; taking a capital shatters its entire empire. If attacker had no empire, use available free capital/star and matching small flag; if none are available, no new empire or flags form. On failure attacker loses one tower.
answers.evidence: Events in India—Invasion Crisis: whole-empire comparison, strict threshold, flag changes and no-flags case.

answers.answer: For non-Company Rebellion, compare only rebelling region strength plus modifier against its sovereign capital strength; other empire regions do not count. It must be strictly greater, so a tie fails. Success makes actor sovereign, removes its flag and closes all its orders (Cascade if already closed); failure removes one tower from the capital.
answers.evidence: Events in India—Rebellion Crisis entry.

answers.answer: On Region Loss, Commander returns half family trophies rounded up and member to supply. Roll one die per Army officer; each 6 removes that officer. Eliminate Governor (card, fatigue and member to supplies), remove overlay, partial Company ship and unrest. Restore dome with one tower (or Foreign Invasion’s specified tower strength) and appropriate invasion flag; return control token with loot side down and region-symbol side up. Future conquest has no loot modifier and region loses Presidency association. Normal Invasion closes orders or Cascades if already closed; Rebellion/Foreign Invasion already close them. Standing loss escalates by number of regions lost so far this turn: first −1, second additional −2, etc. Loss does not automatically remove other Company regions; resolve those attacks and defenses separately.
answers.evidence: Events in India—Region Loss: destinations, checks, token, Standing and independent region-loss rule.

answers.answer: After a successful normal Invasion Crisis, Elephant moves to the successful capital (Imperial Ambitions); after other Marches, it goes to the top-stack region. In a Company region place it fully inside; in dominated region point toward sovereign; in sovereign region point across shape-marked border. If that neighbor is already dominated by actor, use first clockwise neighbor not dominated; if all neighbors are dominated, use redirect-arrow border pointing toward empire capital. The summary does not specify an additional posture for a fully formed empire beyond these destination-region rules.
answers.evidence: Events in India—Elephant’s March: destination and posture for Company/dominated/sovereign regions; no distinct ‘fully formed empire’ posture stated.

answers.answer: Roll storm die to select target Presidency regions: West→Bombay, South→Madras, East→Bengal; all storms means each, none means top-stack region. For each target, ordinary die determines attack strength and, on success, resulting towers are half that roll rounded down. Unrest does not add to primary attack or determine towers, but the event uses Company-defense procedure and secondary unrest attacks. On success close all target orders once (Cascade if already all closed), remove target flag and all matching flags if capital, restore dome if Company controlled, set tower strength as above. Move Elephant with circle shape only if it was fully inside an invaded Company region.
answers.evidence: Events in India—Foreign Invasion and FAQ—Foreign Invasion and unrest: targets, dice, order/flag/map changes, Elephant and ruling.

answers.answer: PM must draw at least one law. After one or two ordinary (non-dilemma) laws, may stop or continue up to three total, then choose any revealed law and discard others. Drawing a dilemma forces selection of that dilemma and ends drawing immediately. Before voting, PM moves dial either direction to the first policy space matching chosen law’s bottom icon; that fixes target and consequence. The summary does not specify more about how a dilemma changes proposed-policy selection.
answers.evidence: Parliament Meets: law drawing and policy selection rules.

answers.answer: Tax: each family pays £1 to bank per target it owns; unpaid target returns to supply, including Chairman if taxed. Window tax additionally charges each window on enterprises and each family member’s prize; if unpaid return enterprise/prize member. Lost shipyard’s fitted ship remains and shipyard cannot be purchased until ship returns; losing prize/luxury removes its VP. Bonus: bank pays each family £1 per target owned. Power: swap target Power marker with next higher; if target already highest, swap any other pair. The summary does not give a separate general rule for choosing a target beyond the policy/law.
answers.evidence: Parliament Meets—Policy table: Tax, Window tax, Bonus, Power.

answers.answer: Starting PM clockwise, players cast votes; each £1 family cash buys one vote plus printed card votes. Each card’s votes may be used only once across entire vote and remain rotated until resolution. PM may call another full round or stop after each; a round with no votes ends voting. Adjust support up/down without track limit. Summary does not state a fixed maximum number of rounds or a separate rule naming who may call more rounds beyond PM.
answers.evidence: Parliament Meets—Voting: purchase, card reuse, round control and stopping condition.

answers.answer: A player who voted for may later oppose; once opposed, they cannot vote for during that vote. Track opposition votes; largest opponent total is Opposition Leader, with tied current holder retaining it. With recipient consent, votes may be cast for someone who already opposed or commits to oppose and count toward their opposition total. PM cannot oppose or consent to enterprises opposing except forced use of ‘Vote with my enterprises’ promise. The summary does not describe a separate selection rule for the initial Opposition Leader beyond having the most opposition votes and tie retention.
answers.evidence: Parliament Meets—Voting: switching restrictions, Opposition Leader, coalition votes and PM exception.

answers.answer: Final turn still pays upkeep for each prize; if unpaid, return that member and lose printed prize VP. Skip Refresh and go to Final Scoring. On nonfinal turns, return writers to associated Presidency Writers boxes, filled tokens/dividers and extra ships to supply; reactivate exhausted Army officers/regiments; exhaust active local alliances without reactivating them; fitted player ships keep fatigue. Advance turn and begin London Season.
answers.evidence: Upkeep and Refresh: per-prize upkeep and final/nonfinal procedure table.

answers.answer: Each shareholder may make one additional London Season retirement from supply (not Pensioners), regardless of number of firms owned. Printed cost cannot exceed the highest total dividend marker among firms they own; no retirement from a firm whose marker is absent/zero. Spouse discounts may permit a higher-cost prize; otherwise normal retirement and prestige eligibility apply. At start of Final Scoring, score firms, then allow one special retirement regardless of Company success/failure, before normal scoring; no display cards in Final Scoring. The summary does not state a separate marker value formula beyond actual recorded total dividend payout.
answers.evidence: Deregulation—Special retirement: limit, eligible piece, marker, discounts and Final Scoring timing; dividends section defines marker.

answers.answer: Investment adds £5 from bank to firm London treasury; firm trade bids are paid from London to bank, and firm ship fitting costs £3 from London to bank. Ship acquisitions use London (buying an already Company ship pays Shipping treasury). Expenses may use either/both London and India; dividends must come from India; trade revenue goes to India. Family cash cannot be transferred into or out of firm treasuries except specified procedures, so it cannot be gifted into firms.
answers.evidence: Deregulation overview: treasury sources/uses and no family transfer; ship rules; firm expenses/dividends and trade sections.

answers.answer: Firms phase occurs after Family share creation and before Hiring, if deregulated. Investments occur without set order until no one wants more; manager resolves timing conflicts within a firm, PM between firms. Strategies are then chosen secretly. During Company Operation each firm reveals strategy at its associated Presidency before any actions; within trade, the initiative rules determine order and ties.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: Firms after Family; Firms phase: investments and conflict resolution; strategies and competing trade timing.

answers.answer: A firm may fit a ship from a shipyard only with shipyard owner consent, paying £3 from London to bank. It may buy a player-owned ship already in Company with owner consent for £3 unfatigued or £2 fatigued, paid into Shipping treasury. Firms cannot acquire Company or extra ships. The summary does not say a firm can fit another player’s ship without consent; the specified fitting rule requires consent.
answers.evidence: Deregulation—Firms phase: investments: ship purchase and fitting rules.

answers.answer: Only a player managing no firm at all may initiate hostile takeover; obtain consent of holders of a majority of target shares. Target’s ships, money and shares move to the initiator’s own charter; copy both cube positions. Former manager returns cubes and flips their board to family side. Managing any other firm makes initiator ineligible.
answers.evidence: Deregulation—Firms phase: investments—Hostile takeover.

answers.answer: Merger requires managers to negotiate with every shareholder’s consent. Highest-Value firm is primary; if tied, players choose among them. Transfer all secondary shares, ships and treasury funds to primary; secondary boards return to family side. Negotiate transfers and any shares over ten returned with those owners’ consent. Entire agreement is one binding immediate transfer. Primary keeps its Value/dividend track; secondary treasuries transfer into it.
answers.evidence: Deregulation—Firms phase: investments—Merger: consent, primary, transfers, cap and track.

answers.answer: Hobnob commits no bid, trade or dividends, but still pays expenses and retains prior dividend marker for retirement. Hobnob ships are exempt from storms. The summary does not state a further Hobnob permission or prohibition beyond these effects.
answers.evidence: Firm strategies: Hobnob choice; storms and firm expenses: Hobnob exceptions.

answers.answer: Yes. Emergency investment uses normal share/workshop contribution rules even when the ten-share cap prevents more shares: firm still receives £5 from bank to London. Pay expenses, lose any remaining cash, and reduce Value one space per emergency investment. Same-turn Company shares remain ineligible for contribution even if traded away; Chairman shares and shares while Standing/Debt lined also remain restricted. The cap prevents shares, not rescue cash.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses, rescue and dividends: emergency investment at ten-share cap, cash use and Value reduction; investment rules on same-turn shares.

answers.answer: Emergency negotiated merger is limited to the endangered firm and only one other firm; all involved shareholders must consent under normal merger procedure. The other firm must first pay its own expenses if not already paid, then cover the endangered firm’s unpaid expenses. This differs from ordinary merger, which can combine multiple firms by agreement before expenses.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses, rescue and dividends: emergency merger one-other-firm and payment order; normal merger procedure.

answers.answer: Voluntary dissolution requires consent of all shareholders and uses insolvent-firm dissolution: shares go to Debtor’s Prison (−1 VP each), ships return to matching shipyards, and charter flips to family side. Invested workshops remain invested for rest of game and are not recovered.
answers.evidence: Firms phase—Voluntary dissolution; firm expense dissolution rules.

answers.answer: Each player totals VP from all firm shares they own across all firms, then rounds their own fractional total down; do not round per share, firm or player. Firm Value per-share score: 1=−1; 2=0; 3–4=½; 5–7=1; 8–9=1½; 10=2. Deduct 1 VP per own family piece in Debtor’s Prison. These firm scores and any eligible special retirement are handled before ordinary Company survival/failure branch; Company failure affects Company shares/workshops separately as usual.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: firm share rate, per-player aggregation/rounding, Debtor’s Prison deduction and order before Company branch.
Setup—Prizes table.

answers.answer: 1710 turns 1–5 and has no deregulation procedures. 1758 turns 3–7 and can vote in deregulation. 1813 turns 5–8 and starts deregulated. Long 1710 turns 1–8 and has deregulation available separately.
answers.evidence: Setup—Scenario figures table and Scenario standard-scope table.

answers.answer: 1710 starts Standing £10 expectations, Debt 0, each office treasury £3, Royal Protection passed, one regiment per Army and no Company ships. 1758 starts £12 expectations, Debt 3, each office treasury £4, Calico Acts, one regiment per Army, one Company ship in East Indian, and Bengal control token in Bengal Presidency.
answers.evidence: Setup—Scenario figures table; 1758 control token noted in scenario table and setup text.

answers.answer: 1813 is turns 5–8, Standing £10 expectations, Debt 0, each office treasury £3; passed laws Military Oversight, Deregulation (Debtor’s Prison side), Calico Acts; two regiments per Army and one Company ship per sea zone. Put +2/−2 share-value token in Court, create China, place Bombay/Madras/Bengal control tokens in their Presidencies, return Governor General law to box, and overlay Governor General over Director of Trade; use Governor General instead of Director and no Governors. Scenario card reverse supplies India map configuration.
answers.evidence: Setup—Scenario figures and 1813-specific setup paragraph.

answers.answer: Final-turn Power awards: turns 1–3: first/second 3/1 VP; turns 4–6: 5/2; turns 7–8: 8/4. Tied first group each receives only the lower award and no other award. Tied second receive none.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions—Power award and ties.

answers.answer: Initial Power positions: Social 2, Company shares 1, Shipping 0, Manufacturing 0. In 1758/Long 1710, Standing £4/6/8 or Debt 5/6/7/8 are lined and allow PM to call Deregulation; Standing £4 or Debt 8 is starred and makes the vote mandatory. S is above £10 on Standing track.
answers.evidence: Setup—Power positions and Deregulation spaces; Deregulation trigger rules.

answers.answer: Unrest does not add to Foreign Invasion’s primary attack strength or determine resulting tower levels. Use ordinary die for both attack strength and halving into towers. Successful invasion closes all target orders once; if all already closed, Cascade; Region Loss does not close them a second time.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings—Foreign Invasion and unrest.

answers.answer: If Mercantile/Diplomatic Connection reduces a check to zero dice, it is failure. Company Fraud occurs at start of Revenue: roll one die per your officeholder, reduce Balance by twice highest roll (minimum zero), and take from bank only the actual Balance reduction, not more than Balance removed. Public Demands Impeachment returns member to supply and office card to vacancies. Military Oversight’s demoted Commander is eligible as an officer for reappointment.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings—Applicable official errata: four corrected card rules.

answers.answer: Shared setup puts Company Balance at £5, family VP markers at zero, local alliances in named Army boxes, and loot tokens money-side up in matching regions. Choose scenario and use its setup card for Standing, Debt, treasuries, laws, regiments, ships and India political map; put Turn marker on its date and PM dial arm at matching date. Scenario card reverse gives exact India map configuration where specified.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1–2: initial Balance, VP, alliances, loot and scenario/date/map placement.

answers.answer: Normal sequence: London Season → Family → Firms if deregulated → Hiring → Company Operation → Bonuses → Revenue → Events in India → Parliament Meets → Upkeep and Refresh. Eligible special Deregulation vote occurs before London Season at turn start. Skip London Season on game’s first turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: phase order, first-turn skip and special vote timing.

answers.answer: Retirement order begins with Chairman, or former Chairman if office vacant, then clockwise. Each player may retire each pensioner (it is optional) to a prize, pays printed cost and gains printed VP; actual spending is set aside to determine display-selection order, then paid to bank after London Season. Unused pensioners return to supply and do not carry over.
answers.evidence: London Season—Retirements: acting order, optionality, prize/cost/VP, money timing and unused pensioners.

answers.answer: No. When an empire loses its last dominated region, remove surviving capital’s starred flag; it is no longer an empire. This applies regardless of cause, including Rebellion or Company conquest of that last dominated region.
answers.evidence: Components—India terminology: last dominated region rule explicitly covers both causes.

answers.answer: Per share by firm Value: 1 = −1 VP; 2 = 0; 3 or 4 = ½; 5, 6 or 7 = 1; 8 or 9 = 1½; 10 = 2. Each player totals their shares across firms and rounds their own fractional total down.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: ‘Firm-track VP per share’ table in prose and firm-score aggregation rule.
